headline: Connecting Google Drive is easy for internal testing, but public apps requiring broad read access face a mandatory security audit costing thousands of dollars.
summary: Developers can immediately test integrations using the 'Testing' mode with up to 100 allowlisted users, though tokens expire every 7 days. Reaching production is straightforward if you limit access to non-sensitive scopes like drive.file. However, requesting restricted scopes (like reading all files) requires a mandatory Cloud App Security Assessment (CASA) by a third-party lab, costing $3,000-$10,000+ and taking up to 6 weeks.

oauth.pkce: Supported. Clients must pass code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256 during authorization, and matching code_verifier during token exchange.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Requires access_type=offline and prompt=consent in the auth request. Expires after 7 days in 'Testing' mode or 6 months of inactivity. Limit of 100 tokens per user per client ID.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Strict character-for-character matching required (no wildcards or fragments). Must use https://, except http:// is allowed for localhost/127.0.0.1. Raw IPs are forbidden.
oauth.scopes: Configured via APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen. Narrow scopes (drive.file) avoid intense review; broad scopes trigger mandatory third-party audits.

stages.name: Initial App Creation and Testing Mode

steps.title: Register App and Obtain Credentials
steps.detail: Create a project in Google Cloud Console, enable the Google Drive API, configure the consent screen to 'External' (Testing status), and generate a Web Application OAuth client ID.

steps.title: Implement PKCE Auth Flow
steps.detail: Write the server-side or local agent code to authorize users with code_challenge (S256) and obtain offline refresh tokens.

steps.title: Verify Domain Ownership
steps.detail: Verify the domain hosting your privacy policy, homepage, and redirect URIs in Google Search Console via the DNS Domain Property method.

steps.title: Draft and Publish Privacy Policy
steps.detail: Publish an HTML privacy policy that explicitly addresses compliance with the Google API Services User Data Policy and Limited Use requirements.

steps.title: Record YouTube Demo Video
steps.detail: Record an unlisted YouTube video showing the full OAuth flow starting from a clean browser, visibly displaying the client ID in the URL bar, and demonstrating app functionality.

steps.title: Submit Verification Request
steps.detail: Submit the OAuth consent screen for production review, providing the demo video, scope justifications, and verified domain links.

steps.title: Wait for Google Review
steps.detail: Google reviews the brand assets and non-sensitive/sensitive scope requests.

steps.title: Engage Third-Party Authorized Lab
steps.detail: If requesting restricted scopes (e.g., drive.readonly), pay an authorized lab $3,000-$10,000+ to conduct a Tier 2 Cloud App Security Assessment (CASA).

steps.title: Complete Audit and Receive LOV
steps.detail: Work with the lab to remediate any security findings and receive a Letter of Validation (LOV) valid for 1 year.

requirements.text: Your redirect URIs, privacy policy, and homepage must reside on a domain verified by a project owner in Google Search Console.
A publicly accessible HTML privacy policy is required, containing explicit Limited Use compliance language.
A YouTube demo video must be provided, visibly displaying the client ID in the browser URL bar during the OAuth flow.
Apps requesting restricted scopes must undergo an annual third-party CASA security assessment to obtain a Letter of Validation.
A written justification is required for every requested scope, explaining why narrower scopes cannot be used.

gotchas.text: Refresh tokens issued to external test users in the 'Testing' publishing status expire automatically after 7 days.
Google limits refresh tokens to 100 per user per client ID; generating a 101st token revokes the oldest one without warning.
Requesting broad restricted scopes (like the full drive scope) when a narrower scope (like drive.file) suffices will result in verification rejection.
Internal Workspace apps bypass external verification and security assessments entirely.

permissions.action: Create new files or access files explicitly opened by the user (via Google Picker)
permissions.review_impact: Requires only standard brand/non-sensitive verification; no third-party audit required.

permissions.action: Store and manage the agent's private application data in a dedicated hidden folder
permissions.review_impact: Requires only standard brand/non-sensitive verification; no third-party audit required.

permissions.action: Search, inspect metadata, and download all files across the user's entire Drive
permissions.review_impact: Triggers restricted scope verification and a mandatory paid CASA Tier 2 security assessment.

permissions.action: Full read, write, create, and delete access across all user files and folders
permissions.review_impact: Triggers restricted scope verification and a mandatory paid CASA Tier 2 security assessment.

permissions.action: List, search, and view file metadata (names, hierarchy) without reading contents
permissions.review_impact: Triggers restricted scope verification and a mandatory paid CASA Tier 2 security assessment.

blockers.issue: You need to test the integration with external users but haven't passed verification or CASA.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Set your OAuth consent screen publishing status to 'Testing' and add up to 100 test user emails to the allowlist. Inform testers they will need to re-authenticate every 7 days due to token expiry.
Downgrade your requested scopes (e.g., from drive to drive.file), update your application to use the Google Picker API for explicit file selection, and resubmit your written justification.

blockers.issue: Verification is stuck because the demo video was rejected.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Record a new unlisted YouTube video. Ensure you start from a clean browser, visibly highlight the client ID in the URL bar during the consent screen, and show exactly how the requested scopes are used in your app.

agent_can: Draft the privacy policy incorporating the required Limited Use compliance clauses.
Write the least-privilege scope justifications for the Google verification review.
Implement the OAuth PKCE flow (code challenge/verifier) and token exchange logic.
Handle Drive API 429 rate limit errors using truncated exponential backoff.
you_must: Create the project and configure the OAuth consent screen in the Google Cloud Console.
Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console using the DNS method.
Record and upload the YouTube demo video showing the OAuth flow and client ID.
Pay a third-party laboratory and undergo a CASA security assessment if using restricted scopes.

key_claims.text: Refresh tokens issued in 'Testing' status expire after 7 days.
Restricted scopes require an annual CASA Tier 2 security assessment costing thousands of dollars.
The authorization endpoint natively supports PKCE with S256.
Drive API quota limit is 325,000 quota units per minute per user.
Google OAuth authorization endpoint is active and enforces strict parameter validation.
